sentences.text: - II, Pathanamthitta are the appellants in MACA No.3171 of 2021.
The 2nd respondent in the O.P is the appellant in MACA No.523 of 2018.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2.

The O.P. was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the mother and the daughter of the deceased by name Sri.Raju, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 24.05.2013.

According to them, on 24.05.2013, at about 07.00 p.m., while the deceased was walking through the public road, an ape pick up van bearing Registration No.KL 09X 769 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, knocked him down.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the next day, ie. on 25.05.2013.
3. The 1st respondent is the owner cum driver, the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle and the 3rd respondent is the wife of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.30,00,000/-.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A13.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.24,24,409/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred MACA No.523 of 2018.
Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the 2 nd respondent preferred MACA No.3171 of 2021.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
9.

Heard Sri.Susanth Shaji, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/claimants, Sri.P.Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the insurance company and Smt.Deepa Sreenivasan, the learned counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent/wife of the deceased.
Though notice was served, 1st respondent did not turn up.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.

One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of Amritha.R vs A.Rajan on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52770159/
4 the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
According to him, the deceased was working as General Extension Officer at Block Panchayat, Chittoor, Palakkad, getting a monthly income of Rs.27,000/-,
but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.20,000/-.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.
11. The learned counsel has relied upon Ext.A8 salary certificate to prove the income of the deceased, which shows that he had a total salary of Rs.26,985/-.
The tribunal has excluded the deductions from the salary and fixed the notional income at Rs.20,000/-.
The above procedure adopted by the Tribunal is not correct.
During the year 2013 -14, there was no income tax for the 1st Rs.1,50,000/- and for the remaining income upto Rs.5,00,000/- tax payable is 10%.
Therefore, the income tax payable for the income of the deceased will come to Rs.5,000/-, the professional tax payable will come to Rs.2,500/-.

Therefore, the monthly income less the income tax and professional tax payable will come to Rs.26,360/-.
12.
On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 51 years.

Therefore, 15% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future MACA NOs. 523 OF 2018 & 3171 OF 2021 2025:KER:32187 prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
and the multiplier to be applied is 11, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009)
6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: Since the deceased was married who left behind 3 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).

In the above circumstance, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.26,67,632/-.
13.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.1,50,000/- towards love and affection, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.20,000/- towards loss of estate.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the above heads are on the higher side.

14. In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.
Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/- each.

Towards loss of consortium,
the petitioners 1 and 2 and 3rd respondent together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,45,200/-
(48,400 x 3).

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, [(2020)9 SCC 644].

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation awarded towards love and affection is to be deducted.
16. During the pendency of the appeal, the 2nd petitioner/Chinna died and the 1st petitioner was impleaded as her sole legal representative.

The learned counsel for the petitioners would argue that,
the 3 rd respondent was living separately from the deceased and the 1st petitioner, that since the 1st petitioner is the sole legal representative of the deceased 2 nd petitioner, her share also is to be Amritha.R vs A.Rajan on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52770159/
5 allotted to the 1 st petitioner.
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would argue that the compensation is to be awarded equally among the 1st petitioner and the 3rd respondent.
17. From the records, it appears that in the claim petition the 3 rd respondent has not joined as one of the claimants and she was accordingly made a respondent.

It appears that, the 1 st petitioner was living along with the 2nd petitioner, the mother of the deceased and the 3 rd respondent was living separately, away from the 1st petitioner as well as the deceased 2nd petitioner.
The 1st petitioner is the sole legal representative of deceased 2 nd petitioner.
The claim petition and the appeal were filed by the petitioners, meeting the MACA NOs. 523 OF 2018 & 3171 OF 2021 2025:KER:32187 expenses from their own pockets.

In the light of the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation can be apportioned among the 1 st petitioner and the 3rd respondent in the ratio 3:2.
18.
According to the learned standing counsel, the 1 st respondent had no valid driving licence at the time of accident.
From Ext.A7 charge sheet also it is seen that the 1st respondent had no valid driving licence and hence he was also charged under Section 3(1) r/w 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though notice was served, the 1st respondent also did not turn up.
Therefore, 2nd respondent is entitled to get an order for recovery of the compensation from the 1st respondent.
19. No change is required in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

20. Therefore, the petitioners along with the 3rd respondent are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.29,54,453/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

as per rules.
